1-3 years Previous work experience in an academic setting.

Under the supervision of the Composition Program Manager, Composition Director and Composition Associate Director, the incumbent contributes to the daily operations of the Composition Program. Responsibilities include: providing administrative assistance to the Composition Program Manager, Director Associate Director and Course Directors, management of the student evaluation process for approximately 600 Composition sections yearly, coordinating the Composition Summer Session Program, and providing assistance with the UCI writing requirement and courses offered in Composition to approximately 9,000 students annually.

Strong interpersonal skills to work and communicate effectively, in person, by email, and by phone, with diverse groups (faculty, staff, administrators, professionals and students) from a wide variety of ethnic, social, and educational backgrounds, to provide information, identify problems, and develop solutions.
Skill in utilizing EEE, UCI's web-based class management system for instructors, teaching assistants, and students.
Proven ability to calculate averages, standard deviations, and other statistics.
Working knowledge of UCI’s policies and procedures.
Technical skills to convert large data sets into summary reports.
Working knowledge of UCI’s schedule of classes and catalogue.

Skill in analyzing information, problems, situations, practices, and procedures to: define the problem or objective; identify relevant concerns or factors; identify patterns, tendencies and relationships, formulate logical and objective conclusions; recognize alternatives and their implications.
Working knowledge of the UC Entry Level Writing Requirement.
Proven skill in the use of a computer using Windows, Microsoft Office (Word and Excel), Eudora for email, and ability to use internet software to access and search the World Wide Web.
Demonstrated ability to write professional correspondence and analytical reports.
Ability to exercise independent thinking and judgment in order to effectively complete assigned projects in a timely manner with minimal direction.
Skills in setting priorities that accurately reflect the importance of job responsibilities.
